title: Computing a function reversibly
objectives: Embed a many-to-one Boolean function in a permutation.
Explain coherent compute, copy and uncompute.
prerequisites: Chapters 3–6: tensor products, unitary gates, joint-state order, coherent control and measurement.

quizzes.question: Why is (x,y)→(x,y⊕f(x)) reversible even for many-to-one f?
options: It retains x, and applying the update twice restores y.
The target is measured halfway through.
feedback: Correct: the full input can be recovered.
f itself need not be injective.

quizzes.question: How is correlated workspace cleaned coherently in compute-copy-uncompute?
options: Apply the inverse computation after copying the basis result to a separate target.
Measure it and assume the useful state stays unchanged.
feedback: Correct: the inverse restores the initialized work registers.
